variants.headline: Builder left unpaid for work done
variants.sub: The builder {builder} is owed payment by the client {client} for completed work.
variants.body:
The client {client} has not paid the builder {builder} for work done. The amount owed is {owed}. After three missed months the builder stops work. For {target}, the event raises the basic question of responsibility when a construction undertaking requires payment as well as performance.

A receivable is not cash received. The builder's work and the client's payment should be distinguished in any account of the undertaking. The stop-work threshold matters, but a prudent manager should not confuse the existence of that rule with evidence that its condition has already been met in this case.

We support {target} against a blanket adverse verdict. The missed payment requires attention, but its existence does not prove every allegation about motives or establish that the project has already reached a stop. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
